blocking.issue: The change table lets any minor release ship a 'Bug fix changing a Revision (with a golden-corpus entry)'. The Configuration model, a foundation document, allows only one exception to byte-for-byte golden-corpus reproduction: a deliberate `ruralz/v1alpha1` default change shipped as a new schema level. Any other change to the serialization needs a new format identifier. This document's own Versioned surfaces row and rule 2 of Ruralz Control upgrades rely on that narrower rule. A digest-changing render or canonicalization fix gated by no schema level breaks 'render at N-1's schema levels and defaults, so a commit yields one digest'. It also breaks the `ruralz bundle push` skew row, and in `ruralz/v1beta1` and `ruralz/v1` it breaks 'defaults never change'. This is the same defect L1-12 raised, and it is still in the text. Here it is flagged as a contradiction with the Configuration model and ADR-0003.
blocking.evidence: Line 41: "| Bug fix changing a Revision (with a golden-corpus entry); new feature, Policy type, CLI verb or flag, metric, error code, field, Host Function or Control Stream field | No | Yes | Yes |". Line 52: "Every release reproduces the golden corpus byte for byte, except entries recording a deliberate default change". Line 171: "renders Revisions at N-1's schema levels and defaults, so a commit yields one digest, feasible because each default change is a new schema level". Configuration model, Canonical form and Revision: "every release MUST reproduce it byte for byte, except entries that record such a change. Changing the serialization requires a new format identifier." ADR-0003 Decision drivers: "on every release except a recorded `v1alpha1` default change".
blocking.fix: Replace the first cell of the line 41 row with "`ruralz/v1alpha1` default change or digest-changing render fix, shipped as a new schema level with a golden-corpus entry; new feature, Policy type, ...". Add one sentence under the table: "In `ruralz/v1beta1` and `ruralz/v1`, a fix that would change a digest ships only behind a new opt-in field or a new format identifier (for example `ruralz.canonical.v2`), per the [Configuration model](../architecture/02-configuration-model.md#canonical-form-and-revision); CI runs the golden corpus at every schema level inside the skew window." In the line 146 `ruralz bundle push` row, change "only if no `ruralz/v1alpha1` default changed" to "only if N added no schema level". If a wider exception is wanted instead, keep the text and add an Open question owned by configuration-model proposing to amend its golden-corpus rule.

non_blocking.section: Control plane and data plane version skew (Ruralz Control upgrades, rule 5)
non_blocking.suggestion: The restore sentence says "Every Node serves detached until the operator supplies a revocation list". It drops the other exit that Control plane and GitOps gives: without a list, pre-restore certificates are refused "until their Nodes re-enroll". Write "until the operator supplies a revocation list or the Node re-enrolls", so operators know re-enrollment also ends detached serving.
